claims.claim: Ulm University chemists used operando spectroscopy to show that the active surface of nickel electrodes in alkaline water electrolysis is nickel dioxide rather than the previously assumed nickel oxyhydroxide.
claims.episode_span: Ulm University chemists used operando spectroscopy to show that the active surface of nickel electrodes in alkaline water electrolysis is nickel dioxide rather than the previously assumed nickel oxyhydroxide.
claims.source_title: Chemists uncover the true active surface of nickel catalysts
claims.supporting_quote: A research team at Ulm University has now refuted a decades-old assumption: The catalytically active surface does not consist of nickel oxyhydroxide (NiOOH), as was previously widely assumed, but is nickel dioxide (NiO₂).
